objective: Qualify the maximum workload's export: review the timeline-scaled render timeout and stacked-layer limit, then implement

parts.part: YU-026c segmented export and resource policy v3

flags: M (200 clips, 16 tracks, ten minutes, 1080p) remains export-unqualified; no limit was raised beyond the reviewed policy
deviations: Design review before code: M's export failed from memory (one FFmpeg pass holds every clip's chain), not time; a stacked-layer cap adds nothing beyond the 16-track limit
Policy v3: exportWallSeconds = min(900, 180 + 30 per started output minute); exportSegmentChains 32; all other values unchanged

Segmented export: frame-aligned windows (down to one frame, at most 48), the picture alone per window, the sound once over the timeline, a stream-copy concat join checked against the exact frame count
Recorded (idle host, one run per profile): S 27 s; T 102 s in 4 segments (now export-qualified); 40-still probe 31 s; worker peaks 12-28% of their limits
M stops at its 480 s limit: no ENOMEM in the windows that ran, but over 2 s per output second, so ten minutes would exceed the reviewed 900 s cap

tests.result: render-segments 6/6: wall formula and cap; frame-aligned contiguous segments at 30 and 24000/1001 fps and the 48 cap; segmented versus single pass with exactly 120 frames, identical frame times, every frame at least 38 dB PSNR and bit-identical sound, with a title across boundaries; ten minutes with sound to its end (18000 frames); a picture-only join; a cancel that leaves no parts
